text:
The Hockey News ran it plainly last week: "Andrew Copp Stepping Up as Nearly All Red Wings Forwards Struggle." That's a fair summary of the 32-year-old's season, and an uncomfortable one for Detroit, a team playing without Dylan Larkin while he holds out for a trade.

Copp has moved into a bigger job, nearly 19.5 minutes a night over his last ten games, and produced eight points in that stretch, seven of them assists. That's about what the chances deserve. The scoring touch hasn't followed: 3 goals on 34 shots in 23 games, 8.8% against a likely range of 9 to 14%.

The worry is the territory. At 5v5 Detroit takes 45% of the expected goals with him on the ice, six points worse than without him, the kind of gap a top-six center can't run for long. Some of that is the role he's been pushed into. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his passing last season (85th percentile in primary shot assists among forwards), and Evolving-Hockey warned that his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances. Useful player, stretched thin.
